messages.content: We got 612 survey responses. 330 are promoters (9-10), 120 are passives, and 162 are detractors (0-6). What is our NPS?
NPS = %promoters minus %detractors = 330/612 (53.9%) minus 162/612 (26.5%), which is about 41. By segment, enterprise comes out at 52 and SMB at 33.
Do the passive responses affect the NPS?
They count in the base of 612 but in neither the promoter nor the detractor side, so they dilute the NPS toward zero. The 120 passives are 19.6% of responses.

I found that 85 of the responses were test submissions from our QA team. After removing them I recalculated the overall NPS myself: 38 on 527 responses. I have not recomputed the segments. Update me, based only on that.

required_facts: The overall NPS is now 38 on 527 responses (recalculated by the user) instead of 41 on 612, so the earlier figure was overstated by about 3 points
The segment figures (enterprise 52, SMB 33) were computed with the test submissions included, so they are not reliable until recomputed
It is not known which segment the QA responses were in, so the direction of the change in each segment is unknown
critical_omissions: Saying the segment figures are still valid
Claiming to have recalculated the NPS or the segments
unnecessary_repetition: The NPS formula and the promoter and detractor percentages
The initial counts of promoters, passives and detractors
